clue.text: Report embargo by German leader

parts.note: an embargo is a ban on trade

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of German

explanation.surface: A news report on a trade embargo announced by Germany's chancellor.
explanation.definitionFit: A report can be a loud explosive noise, as in the report of a gun, which is a bang.

clue.text: A tiny bit of sex appeal heartens yours truly

indicators.note: read as 'goes into the heart of', so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: yours truly is a jokey way of saying 'me', the speaker
IT is old slang for sex appeal, from the 1927 film starring Clara Bow

explanation.surface: Someone is cheered by being found just a little bit attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: A mite is a very small amount or creature, a synonym for a tiny bit.

clue.text: Not in favour of laying a snare

parts.note: a gin is a trap or snare for catching game

explanation.surface: Someone objects to setting traps for animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Agin is a dialect form of 'against', meaning opposed to something.

clue.text: He makes a rector go astray

indicators.note: to go astray is to wander off course, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A man leads a clergyman into sin.
explanation.definitionFit: A creator is one who makes something, especially God as maker of all things.

clue.text: Crazy reason for getting a railway engine

parts.note: loco is slang for crazy
a motive is a reason for doing something

explanation.surface: Someone asks what mad motive could lie behind acquiring a train engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A locomotive is the powered vehicle that pulls a train, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Mother stayed on and played hookey

parts.note: Ma is an informal name for one's mother
to linger is to stay on longer than necessary

explanation.surface: A mother hung around while her child skipped school.
explanation.definitionFit: To play hookey is to dodge school or work, which is to shirk duty by feigning illness, a near synonym.

clue.text: An insomniac's Utopia?

parts.note: someone who cannot sleep would see the land of sleep and dreams as an ideal place

explanation.definitionFit: Dreamland is the imaginary realm of sleep, a paradise for anyone unable to drop off.

clue.text: Boast made by a high flier

definitions.meaning: to boast is to brag or gloat
a bird that flies, here a common black one

explanation.surface: Bragging done by a successful high achiever.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to boast, and the crow is also a black bird that flies high.

clue.text: Film producer arrived with fellow from the Artillery

parts.note: came is the past tense of come, meaning arrived
RA is the Royal Artillery
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A movie producer turns up accompanied by an ex-soldier from the gunners.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameraman operates a film camera, so in a literal sense produces the film footage.

clue.text: Naive pledge to provide fruit

parts.note: green means inexperienced or naive
a gage is something given as a pledge or security

explanation.surface: An innocent promise is made to supply fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A greengage is a type of green plum, an example of fruit.

clue.text: The Spanish consume English fish

indicators.note: to consume is to take in, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: el is Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: Spaniards eat English fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An eel is a long snakelike fish, an example of the category.

clue.text: Bad temper results from recurrent disaster

indicators.note: read as 'running back', so the word for disaster is turned around

parts.note: doom is ruin or disaster

explanation.surface: Repeated calamities leave someone in a foul humour.
explanation.definitionFit: A mood can mean a fit of bad temper or sulkiness, as in 'he's in one of his moods'.

clue.text: An expert offers unbeatable service

definitions.meaning: an expert or star performer
in tennis, a serve the receiver cannot touch

explanation.surface: A skilled player delivers a serve nobody can return.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace is a highly skilled person, and in tennis it is a serve that wins the point untouched.

clue.text: The pantry clearly isn't full

definitions.meaning: a storeroom for food and drinks in a large house
there is evidently space left, read as a two-word phrase

explanation.surface: A remark that the larder obviously has space left in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A still room was a room in a large house where preserves and drinks were made and kept, a kind of pantry.

clue.text: TT teams consist of cheerless chaps

parts.note: TT means teetotal, so sober
sides are teams in a game

explanation.surface: Teams of non-drinkers are made up of gloomy men.
explanation.definitionFit: A sobersides is a solemn, humourless person, so the plural fits cheerless chaps.

clue.text: Wearing a hat whilst cruising

parts.note: in means wearing, as in 'in a coat'
a hat is gear for the top of the head

explanation.surface: Someone drives along with a hat on.
explanation.definitionFit: In top gear means moving at full speed or running smoothly, as a car cruising does.

clue.text: Only Socialists are undisturbed

parts.note: socialists are the political left
alone means only, as in 'he alone knew'

explanation.surface: A political claim that only the left are untroubled.
explanation.definitionFit: Left alone means not interfered with, a synonym for undisturbed.

clue.text: Swindle a man on board

definitions.meaning: to swindle is to cheat or con
a chess piece, also called a castle

explanation.surface: Cheating a fellow passenger on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook is to cheat, and a rook is a piece in chess.

clue.text: A piece missing? That's not good enough

definitions.meaning: read literally, a small portion has been removed
a protest that something is unfair or unacceptable

explanation.surface: Someone complains that part of their order is absent.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit off is British slang for unfair or out of order, and literally a piece removed.

clue.text: Local worker has to stop a girl entering

parts.note: to bar is to stop or block
a maid is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood employee must block a young woman from coming in.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is British slang for one's regular neighbourhood pub, so a local worker serves drinks there.
explanation.definitionFit: A barmaid serves drinks in a pub, and the local is one's nearby pub.

clue.text: Terse, uppish agreement to give respectful greeting

parts.note: curt means brief and terse

indicators.note: in a down clue, upward means read from the bottom, so the word is turned around

parts.note: yes expresses agreement

explanation.surface: A snooty, clipped 'yes' given in place of a polite bow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terse' looks like it describes the speaker's manner, but it supplies a synonym; 'uppish' signals a turnaround because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtsey is a bob made by a woman as a respectful greeting.

clue.text: Short cut used by a horseman

definitions.meaning: a close haircut
a short riding whip

explanation.surface: A rider takes a quicker route.
explanation.definitionFit: A crop is a short haircut, and also a riding whip carried by horsemen.

clue.text: A great deal excited Duncan in Lincoln

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: Abe was the nickname of US president Abraham Lincoln

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Duncan got very worked up while visiting Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln looks like the English city, but here it is the US president, known by his short first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundance means a plentiful quantity, which is a great deal of something.

clue.text: The main factor in Cleo Cleopatra's passing

definitions.text: The main factor in Cleo Cleopatra's passing

parts.words: The main factor in Cleo Cleopatra's passing
parts.note: Cleopatra is said to have died from the bite of a snake held to her breast

explanation.definitionFit: Legend says Cleopatra killed herself with the bite of an Egyptian cobra, a small venomous snake.

clue.text: Hair-styler used by society girl

definitions.meaning: a product applied to hair to hold its style
the upper-class pronunciation of 'girl', used for a posh young woman

explanation.surface: A debutante uses a styling product on her hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Gel is a hair product, and 'gel' is how a posh accent says girl.

clue.text: Failing to find a deputy

definitions.meaning: a fault or moral weakness
one standing in for another

explanation.surface: Someone is unable to locate a stand-in.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice is a moral failing, and vice also means a deputy, as in vice-president.

clue.text: His aim is to soothe Pat by manipulation

definitions.text: His aim is to soothe Pat by manipulation

indicators.note: manipulation means handling and rearranging, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A practitioner's goal is to relieve Pat's pain by working on the body.
explanation.definitionFit: An osteopath treats pain by manipulating bones and muscles, so the whole clue describes one.

clue.text: German king unaffected by reversal

indicators.note: the word reads the same backwards as forwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A German monarch who cannot be overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto I was a German king and Holy Roman Emperor, a name borne by several German rulers.

clue.text: Broadcasts songs

definitions.meaning: transmits on radio or television
tunes or melodies

explanation.surface: A radio station transmits music.
explanation.definitionFit: To air is to broadcast, and airs are tunes or songs.

clue.text: Can't bear to see Henry brewing tea

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

indicators.note: brewing means being made up, so these letters are stirred

explanation.surface: Someone cannot stand watching Henry make the tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To hate something is to be unable to bear it, a synonymous phrase.

clue.text: Sweetie, that's not cheap

definitions.meaning: a term of endearment like darling
expensive, high in price

explanation.surface: A partner is told, darling, that it was expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear is a term of endearment, and dear also means expensive.

clue.text: The voters choose to speak

parts.note: to elect is to choose by vote
to orate is to speak formally

explanation.surface: The public choose who gets to make speeches.
explanation.definitionFit: The electorate is the whole body of people entitled to vote.
